records.issue_text: Legacy flexbox prefixes (2009-spec box properties) don't support `margin-left: auto` alignment or the ordering model used, giving false compatibility and broken header layout in old browsers
records.rationale: The diff adds legacy 2009-spec flexbox prefixes via `@mixin flexbox()` (`display: -webkit-box; display: -moz-box; ...`) and uses modern flex alignment patterns in the same rules, e.g. `.panel { margin-left: auto; @include order(3); }` after removing `float: right;` in `header.scss`. In old `-webkit-box`/`-moz-box` implementations, auto margins and the ordering model (`-webkit-box-ordinal-group`) do not behave the same as modern flexbox, so these prefixes can create a false sense of compatibility and can lead to misaligned/incorrect header layout in those legacy browsers.

records.issue_text: Making .contents a flex container invalidates remaining float children (plugin/theme float styling on .extra-info-wrapper or .panel), causing unpredictable rendering, with overlap in old WebKit
records.rationale: The diff makes `.contents` a flex container (`@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);` in `header.scss`). In flex layout, `float` on *direct flex items* no longer affects positioning, so any plugin/theme CSS that still relies on `float` for elements inside `.contents` (e.g., re-adding `float` to `.panel`, or other children not shown here) could stop working or render differently.
